A horizontal bar chart showing the relative amount of precipitate formed when rabbit anti-human serum is mixed with serum from different animals. Bars from longest to shortest: human (100), chimpanzee (very long, slightly shorter than human), gorilla (very long), baboon (Old World monkey, medium-long), spider monkey (New World monkey, medium), dog (short), pig (short), chicken (almost none). Beside the chart, a small row of test tubes with decreasing cloudiness. The bar lengths show the pattern only, no exact numbers other than human = 100.

An evolutionary tree of animals drawn as a branching tree on a soft background. At the base: a single-celled protozoan (Amoeba). Branches rising in order: Hydra (coelenterate), tapeworm (flatworm), roundworm (nematode), earthworm (annelid), then a branch splitting to an insect (arthropod) and a snail (mollusc). A main trunk continues to vertebrates: a fish, then a frog (amphibian), then a lizard (reptile), which splits into two branches ending in a bird and a mammal (goat). Water shown at the lower part of the tree, land above.

Diagram of the sickle-cell mutation in three linked rows. Top row: two short DNA strands side by side as coloured base sequences, normal (…C T G A G G…) and sickle (…C T G T G G…), with the single changed base A to T highlighted in red. Middle row: the corresponding short chains of amino acid beads, with the sixth bead (blue) in the normal chain and "valine" (red) in the sickle chain. Bottom row: a normal round biconcave red blood cell beside a sickle-shaped red blood cell.
